slides.title: Maus Crepe Insights
slides.hook: We turned 828 robot crepe runs into measurements, models and next experiments.
slides.notes: Open in one line: Maus robots make crepes on their own, every run is logged, and we turned those logs into measurements, models and next experiments. Everything in this deck comes from the repository's own documentation, its model cards, or a private data export. The repository is public; the Maus run data is not.

slides.title: What we built
caveats: Honest read: three of four check heads do not generalize (balanced accuracy 0.67 to 0.92 on 31 to 61 frame holdouts).
fold-class scores 0.99 on 110 frames, but on weak labels; quarter recall drops to 0.02 of 82 frames when maus-quin is held out.
690 of the 828 runs have no camera measurement at all - checks only exist from 13 October, so they are unmeasured, not evidence.
slides.notes: Four headline numbers, then the honest read said plainly. 828 runs logged, 138 vision-scored. Four check-verdict heads plus a fold-class model. The caveats are the point: three of four check heads do not generalize, fold-class is 0.99 on weak labels and collapses on a held-out robot, and 690 of 828 runs have no camera measurement because checks only exist from 13 October.

slides.title: See it live

bullets.text: Ask: more check records, because 117 of the 148 failed runs have none, and about 140 to 150 interleaved runs per robot, to turn the open questions into answers.

slides.footer: Public repo; the Maus run data stays out of Git
slides.notes: The repository is public at github.com/leonardoAB1/maus-crepe-insights, and there is a live site - the placeholder link in the deck still needs the real URL dropped in. The ask is one line: more check records and interleaved runs per robot, which is what turns every 'we cannot tell yet' into an answer. We never send anything to a robot; the next batch is a run sheet a person runs by hand.
